name: module_scan
description: Use when you need the fault codes or part / software numbers of the car's other control modules (ABS, cluster, gearbox, ...), not just the engine.
instructions: Read the scan_modules section of the triage step first: triage already scanned every UDS module once. Do not repeat a full scan in the same run.
When the symptom points to one system, call scan_modules with only those addresses to re-check them, e.g. {"addresses":["03"]} for ABS / ESP or {"addresses":["01"]} for the engine.
Look up a module code that matters with read_dtcs_detail when it is a P code; C, B and U codes are described by their system (chassis, body, network).
TP2.0 modules (older VAG bus) are never read by the agent. Use the saved-scan line as it is, quote its date, and tell the user to run Module scan for a fresh read.
interpret: Each code carries the ISO 14229 status byte: bit 0 (0x01) test failed now, bit 2 (0x04) pending, bit 3 (0x08) confirmed, bit 7 (0x80) the module asks for a warning lamp. 0x09 = failing now and confirmed; 0x08 = confirmed but not failing now (history); 0x04 alone = pending.
Pending: seen on the current or last drive cycle but not confirmed yet; intermittent or just starting. Confirmed: stored on enough cycles to count as a real fault.
The VAG 5-digit number (VCDS) of a P code is its two bytes in decimal; use it to match VCDS logs.
A module with no answer is not proof of a fault: it may be absent, asleep, behind TP2.0 or on an address the profile has not confirmed. Do not name it faulty on that alone.
Lines marked unconfirmed come from module addressing not yet checked on this car: treat their codes as a lead to confirm, not as evidence.
Network (U) codes in several modules at once usually share one cause: low battery voltage during cranking, a gateway or a bus wiring fault. Check the battery first.
Airbag (15) and immobilizer (25) are outside the agent's scope; tell the user to read them with a dedicated tool if the symptom involves them.
